title: Senegal faces Mozambique in 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers
subtitle: The match opens Group J’s first round, featuring venue changes and key absences
excerpt: Senegal and Mozambique will clash this Friday at 3 p.m. in the Zimpeto National Stadium, kicking off the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualification campaign.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Senegal and Mozambique will meet this Friday at 3 p.m. in the Zimpeto National Stadium to open the first round of Group J in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers. The match is highlighted because the home venue, which should have belonged to Senegal, has been reversed and will be played on Mozambican soil, altering the tactical reading of the encounter.

Reasons for the venue reversal and technical expectations

Although Senegal is the official home team, the match will be held in Maputo, creating an atypical scenario for the Senegalese side, used to playing at home. Available indicators point to Senegalese control, but the absence of two key forwards – Ismaila Sarr and Iliman Ndiaye, suspended for two matches – leaves head coach Patrick Vieira with the option to call on youngsters such as Ibrahim Mbaye (Aston Villa) and options like Abdallah Sima or Assane Diao.

Recent history between the teams

In the last five encounters, Senegal has three wins and two draws, without suffering a defeat. The most recent match, in the 2023 AFCON qualifiers, ended with a 1‑0 Senegalese victory in Maputo, after a 5‑1 rout in Dakar four days earlier. The aggregate score of these meetings underscores the disparity: nine goals for Senegal against three for Mozambique.

Probable line‑ups and key absences

Senegal is expected to line up a 4‑3‑3 with Yehvann Diouf; Nobel Mendy, Kalidou Koulibaly, Moussa Niakhaté and El Hadji Malick Diouf; Idrissa Gana Gueye, Lamine Camara and Pape Matar Sarr; Ibrahim Mbaye, Nicolas Jackson and Abdallah Sima. In addition to the suspensions, Sadio Mané is out with a physical issue and Édouard Mendy has retired from the national team, passing the starting role to Diouf.

Mozambique, under Chiquinho Conde, is expected to use a 4‑4‑2 with Ernan Siluane; Feliciano Jone, Edmilson Dove, Bruno Langa and Valter Nhacussa; Geny Catamo, Ricardo Guimarães, Manuel Kambala, Alfonso Amade; Faizal Bangal and Chamito Lamborino. The absences of Diogo Calila (foot fracture) and Stanley Ratifo (knee problem) were announced the day before, reducing options for left‑back and striker. Newcomers José Guirrugo, Bruno Wilson and Cândido Mathe were called up but are not favorites to start the match.

Tactical challenges for the Mambas

Mozambique should prioritize defensive compactness and speed in transitions, with Edmilson Dove anchoring the defense and Geny Catamo open on the right to exploit counter‑attacks. The absence of Calila and Ratifo concentrates offensive responsibility on Catamo, who is the main Mozambican representative in major European leagues.

Result forecast and implications

Performance indicators and the 85‑point FIFA ranking gap point to a Senegal victory, projected at 2‑0. The encounter serves as the first test of Vieira’s new phase, which includes 12 debutants, and as an opportunity for Chiquinho Conde to demonstrate the progress of the project built since 2021, which already earned qualification for the 2023 AFCON and the first quarter‑final appearance in 2025.

With information from LANCE!, MZNews, Jornal Desafio.
